findings.claim: Chart-switching geodesic integration is ready for tool paths over physical parts

hypothesis: An atlas of charts with exact transitions through the embedding integrates geodesics through or near a chart's coordinate singularity with an accuracy that does not depend on how close they pass, while a single chart loses accuracy or fails near its singular point. Shown for the two-chart polar atlas of the sphere (great circles through and near a pole) and for the Monge-plus-polar atlas of the Gaussian bump built from a ChartMap (geodesics through and near the apex).
input_data: unit sphere; great circles with closest approach delta in [0.0, 0.1, 0.01, 0.001, 0.0001, 1e-06, 1e-08, 1e-10, 1e-12] to the north pole, azimuth 1.3, full length 2 pi
exact meridian in chart A alone at 101 step counts (350..450)
256 + 4096 seeded sphere points for transitions and covering (seed 3337)

Gaussian bump h = 0.5, sigma = 1: geodesics from x = -1.5 at offset delta in [0.0, 0.1, 0.01, 0.001, 0.0001, 1e-06, 1e-08] from the apex, length 3.0, RK4 200 steps, reference Monge chart alone at 800 steps; 256 seeded points of the Monge disc of radius 2.0 (seed 3661)
interface under test: ciw.lab.surfaces and ciw.lab.integrators at the source digests recorded in provider_runtime_identity.sources
mathematical_model: Atlas: charts X_c with closed-form inverses; u_B = X_B^{-1}(X_A(u_A)), v_B = g_B^{-1} J_B^T J_A v_A; regularity lambda_min / lambda_max of g (scale free); switch between RK4 steps when the active chart's regularity < 1/4. Sphere: chart A X = R(sin t cos p, sin t sin p, cos t), chart B = R_y(pi/2) X_A; regularity sin^2 theta = det g / R^4 in each chart and sin^2 theta_A + sin^2 theta_B = 1 + y^2/R^2 >= 1, so the better chart always has regularity >= 1/2. Graph z = f(x, y): Monge chart g = I + grad f grad f^T with regularity 1/(1 + |grad f|^2), and the polar chart (r, t) pulled back through PolarChart, singular at r = 0.
numerical_result: sphere atlas through the pole: error 4.86e-08, 4 switches (A->B, B->A, A->B, B->A); atlas error spread over delta 1.21x; orders 4.16, 3.96; single chart failed for 4 and degraded (>10x atlas) for 7 of 8 delta > 0; exact meridian in chart A alone at 400 steps: error 7.42e-14 with |v_phi| up to 2.47e-10 from rounding; over 101 step counts the 5 runs with a step point within 1e-4 of a pole fail (1) or err >= 2.1e-08, the others err <= 1.19e-10; transitions round trip 6.5e-16, speed 5.25e-16, Jacobian 3.72e-10; covering bound 0.502. Gaussian-bump atlas: error <= 4.05e-09 for every delta (Monge chart alone 6.11e-11), polar chart alone failed for 2 and degraded for 6 of 6 delta > 0; transitions round trip 6e-16, speed 8.17e-16, Jacobian 3.02e-10.
observation_model: Ambient error max_s |X_num(s) - X_ref(s)|: exact great circle cos(s) X0 + sin(s) T0 on the sphere, the refined Monge-chart run on the bump.

title: Add chart-transition support.
uncertainty: Atlas errors are RK4 truncation errors (order 4); the 400-step sphere error differs from the fourth-order predictions of the 200- and 800-step runs by 11.7%. Single-chart errors for small delta come from the unresolved azimuthal rate 1/sin(delta) at a fixed step; the failure steps and the errors for delta <= 1e-8 depend on rounding and may differ across platforms. On the exact meridian the single-chart result depends on the step grid: rounding in g_12 seeds an angular momentum sin^2(theta) v_phi that each pole crossing amplifies, so the 400-step success is a property of that grid (closest step point 0.00531 from a pole), not of the chart.
unresolved_assumptions: An atlas needs an embedding and a closed-form inverse for each chart; atlases are built here for the sphere (rotated polar charts) and for graph surfaces (Monge chart and its polar ChartMap); intrinsic charts such as the hyperbolic plane are not covered.
Switching happens between steps; an adaptive integrator would need event location at the threshold.
The recorded minimum regularity of the active chart restates the switch threshold and the covering bound; it is reported, not checked.
